`check_url_namespaces_unique` collects every chain of instance namespaces in the tree, each namespace joined to those above it with colons, and warns of any that occurs more than once (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_url_namespaces_unique`).
`check_url_settings` looks at `settings.STATIC_URL` and `settings.MEDIA_URL`, each of which must end in a slash if it is set (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_url_settings`).

For each of the four it asks the root resolver for the view and tests whether the view can be called with positional arguments alone: two, the request and the exception, or for the 500 view one (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_custom_error_handlers`).
The route for the lifts is taken as a route, escaped, and matched as literal text too (`django/urls/resolvers.py:_route_to_regex`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:RoutePattern.match`).

The view for the tour is a class, which is callable, so `path` accepted it; what would be called with a request is the class itself (`django/urls/conf.py:_path`).

`"urls.W001"` does not say what the `$` does: the patterns under the include are left only the empty string, or a final newline, to match (`django/urls/resolvers.py:RegexPattern._check_include_trailing_dollar`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:RegexPattern.match`).

`"urls.W002"` is not given when `settings.APPEND_SLASH` is false, nor where a regular expression, or an include's route, ends in a slash too (`django/urls/resolvers.py:CheckURLMixin._check_pattern_startswith_slash`).

`"urls.E008"` says that a handler's view could not be imported even of a value that is not a view at all, which `get_callable`, the function that turns a handler into its view, refuses (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_custom_error_handlers`, `django/urls/utils.py:get_callable`).

`"urls.E009"` is given only for a subclass of `View`, and any other class passes (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern._check_callback`).

A resolver's own matcher is checked only when everything under it is clean: `URLResolver.check` asks its matcher only when its entries produced no message (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.check`).

The handler passes the exception by keyword, as an argument named exception, and the check tries positional arguments alone ([The error views](../views/errors.md)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`).

`simplify_regex` rewrites such an address for a person to read (`django/urls/utils.py:simplify_regex`).

A named group passed over can be taken for an unnamed one: `"^(?P<year>[0-9]{4})(?P<month>[0-9]{2})/$"` comes out as `"/<year><var>/"`, and listurls and the index of views show the address so (`django/urls/utils.py:_find_groups`).

It makes a row of each tuple: the address made readable, the view named by its module and name, and the pattern's name with its instance namespaces joined in front by colons, which is the name it is reversed by; the rows are sorted unless it is told otherwise (`django/core/management/commands/listurls.py:Command.get_url_patterns`, `django/core/management/commands/listurls.py:Command.handle`).

**Trap.** listurls lists the module that `ROOT_URLCONF` names, which it imports itself: a URLconf that a middleware gives a request in its attribute `"urlconf"` is not listed ([The script prefix, the current URLconf and the caches](state.md#the-current-urlconf)) (`django/core/management/commands/listurls.py:Command.get_url_patterns`).

`BaseCommand.execute` activates none, so from the command line `get_language` falls back to `settings.LANGUAGE_CODE`, and the rows carry that language's prefix, or none under `prefix_default_language=False`; under `call_command`, the caller's (`django/core/management/base.py:BaseCommand.execute`, `django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_language`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:LocalePrefixPattern.language_prefix`).
